items.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued September 7 at 8:40PM PDT until September 8 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
items.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 4 to 7 feet with sets up to 9
feet, highest at south and southwest-facing beaches. Strong
and dangerous rip and longshore currents. Minor coastal
flooding from a combination of high surf and high astronomical
tides during the evenings.

* WHERE...Beaches of Orange and San Diego Counties.

* WHEN...Through 11 PM PDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with isolated
road closures expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing
conditions and beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Predicted higher high tides:

Newport Beach: Tuesday: 7.0 feet at 7:59 PM.

La Jolla: Tuesday: High 6.9 feet at 7:54 PM PDT.
items.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

items.headline: Heat Advisory issued September 7 at 8:16PM PDT until September 10 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
items.description:
* WHAT...High temperatures 85 to 95 degrees expected and overnight
lows in the mid 70s.

* WHERE...Orange County Coastal Areas and San Diego County Coastal
Areas.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Tuesday to 8 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Moderate to major HeatRisk. Elevated overnight
lows will limit relief from the heat.
items.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.
